transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Ruth Vargas (Sterling CISO), Daniel Kim (Head of AI Platforms), Aisha Mahmood (Compliance)

Summary: quick discovery about where Sterling can run inference (hosted vs dedicated vs private), what controls they need for regulated financial workloads, and next steps to validate with a pilot.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Maya from Redwood, this is Liam our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Ruth: Good, thanks. We're keen to go through data residency and controls, we've got a few internal regs.
[00:12] Daniel: Yup, we've been evaluating options — OpenAI for some prototypes, but for anything customer-sensitive we can't have data leave certain geos or be logged in raw form.
[00:20] Liam: Totally. Just to set expectations, we support three main modes: Redwood Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Redwood Private which can be VPC or on-prem. Each has different guarantees around isolation and logging.
[00:32] Aisha: Can you clarify "Private" — is that fully air-gapped or just VPC peering?
[00:37] Liam: Good question. We do both depending on the customer. Private can be deployed into your VPC with our control plane in a customer-managed network, or an on-prem package for air-gapped requirements. For regulated banks that want keys and logs to stay in their control we usually recommend Private or Dedicated with strict network peering.
[00:54] Ruth: What about logging? Our policy says no full-text logs of customer PII, and retention must be under our control.
[01:02] Maya: We hear that a lot. For Hosted we can redact inputs and avoid persisting full transcripts, but Hosted is still multi-tenant and logs may exist in our control plane for short durations. Dedicated gives more control — you can opt out of retaining full request bodies and enable token-level anonymization. Private gives you total control: logs stay in your KMS and S3 or on-prem storage.
[01:24] Daniel: Any limits around streaming or function calls? We do a lot of tool-calling and structured outputs — latency is a huge factor.
[01:31] Liam: Function calling and streaming are supported across modes. For latency-sensitive paths we suggest Dedicated with reserved capacity and tuned batching/kv-cache settings. There's a tradeoff: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor latency but costs more.
[01:45] Ruth: On compliance: SOC2 and ISO — do you have reports we can review? Also HIPAA, we have some workloads that are HIPAA-adjacent.
[01:54] Maya: Yes. We'll share SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs. For HIPAA, Redwood can sign a BAA for Private deployments; Hosted is trickier unless specific contractual provisions are in place. We'll attach our security deck and the BAA template.
[02:10] Aisha: Encryption at rest and in transit — KMS integration? HSM?
[02:15] Liam: We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for Private and Dedicated. For on-prem air-gapped installs we can support HSM-backed keys. In Hosted our keys are managed by Redwood by default but we offer customer-managed keys for enterprise tiers.
[02:33] Daniel: Data residency: we need processing to occur entirely within EU for EU customers. Is regional hosting available?
[02:38] Maya: Yes, we have region options — Hosted in region for some models and Dedicated/Private you can choose the region or bring your own infra in that region. For strict GDPR processing, Private is best.
[02:51] Ruth: Logging restrictions: we need to prevent retention of raw prompts, but we still need audit logs showing who called what model and when. Can you produce structured audit logs without the prompt text?
[03:01] Liam: Absolutely. Audit logs can be structured metadata only — user_id, route, model_version, latency, status — without the textual prompt. That can be shipped to your SIEM. For forensic needs you can enable encrypted audit artifacts with access controls.
[03:16] Aisha: Who can access logs at Redwood? We need strict RBAC and separation of duties.
[03:22] Maya: We have RBAC, and for Dedicated/Private we can restrict Redwood personnel access entirely; for Hosted we maintain access controls and can provide audit trails of any support access.
[03:34] Daniel: Are there any gotchas around KV cache or prefix caching — sometimes cached context could leak customer data across requests.
[03:41] Liam: We treat KV cache as tenant-isolated. For Dedicated and Private it's inside your tenant boundary. For Hosted, we isolate per customer logically, but if you have very strict requirements we recommend disabling long-term prefix caching or using Private. Sometimes the speech-to-text transcriber says "KV cash" in notes, but it's KV cache.
[03:58] Ruth: Regarding pen-testing and audits — can we run our own pen tests?
[04:03] Maya: Yes, we have a pen-test process and a pre-approved set of tests; for Dedicated/Private we can be more flexible. We also provide a contact for scheduling and scope.
[04:15] Aisha: HIPAA again — you said BAA for Private. If we go Dedicated but managed by Redwood in our cloud account, is that enough or do we need Private?
[04:26] Liam: Dedicated in your VPC with customer-managed keys and no log retention can often meet HIPAA, but legal teams differ. We typically recommend Private/on-prem for the most conservative posture. We'll help draft proposed controls for your legal review.
[04:41] Daniel: Cost question — what's the delta between Hosted and Dedicated? Rough numbers are fine.
[04:46] Maya: Hosted is usage-based per token — typically lowest entry cost. Dedicated has reserved monthly commit for GPUs — higher base cost but better unit economics for high throughput and predictable latency. We'll send example pricing for your workload after you share expected QPS and sequence lengths.
[05:01] Ruth: We need a pilot to validate latency and confirm logs don't leak sensitive info. How long does a pilot usually run?
[05:08] Liam: 2\u20134 weeks is typical. We can spin up a small Dedicated pool or a Private eval in your infra for the pilot. We'll run the benchmark harness and share latency/cost per token and propose tuning (quantization / batching / KV settings).
[05:22] Aisha: Any regulatory reference documents for financial services you can share?
[05:26] Maya: Yes, we'll include our financial services controls pack + sample contracts.
[05:31] Daniel: Network: we'll need IP allowlisting and peering. Can Redwood support direct connect / private peering?
[05:38] Liam: Yes — direct connect, private peering, and VPC peering are supported for Dedicated and Private. We'll need your networking team's contact.
[05:46] Ruth: One more: data deletion — how fast can you purge data? Our policy says 48 hours for certain categories.
[05:52] Liam: For Hosted we have retention windows but can configure faster deletion for enterprise customers; for Dedicated/Private you control the storage and deletion timeline. We'll document the purging APIs.
[06:03] Maya: Great. I'll summarize next steps in an email — we'll attach SOC2/ISO, security deck, and BAAs. We'll also propose dates for the pilot.
[06:12] Daniel: Sounds good. Also loop in our infra lead Tom for peering details.
[06:16] Ruth: We'll push a compliance questionnaire by Monday.
[06:19] Maya: Perfect — thanks everyone.

[06:30] End notes: there were a few audio artifacts and auto-transcription swapped some acronyms (e.g., KV cache -> KV cash, VPC sometimes spelled out). Overall medium transcription quality.
